summary.text: Paul Tonko is the incumbent U.S. Representative for New York's 20th Congressional District, first elected in 2008 and now in his ninth term. An engineer by training, he served on a county board and in the New York State Assembly for 25 years, and led the state energy research authority, before entering Congress. He is the Ranking Member of the Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Environment and sits on the House Budget Committee.

paragraphs.text: Paul Tonko was born in Amsterdam, New York, in 1949 and earned a bachelor's degree in industrial and mechanical engineering from Clarkson University in 1971.

He worked as a public works engineer and state transportation agency employee, according to Ballotpedia; his official speaking biography describes him as a former engineer for the New York State Public Service Commission.
He served on the Montgomery County Board of Supervisors from 1976 to 1983, as chairman in 1981.
Tonko served in the New York State Assembly from 1983 to 2007, and his official biography says he spent 15 of those 25 years as Chairman of the Committee on Energy.
From 2007 to 2008 he was president and CEO of the New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA).

He stepped down from NYSERDA in April 2008 after Rep. Michael McNulty announced his retirement, won the September 2008 Democratic primary for the 21st District over four other candidates, and won the November 2008 general election against Republican James Buhrmaster. He was sworn in on January 3, 2009.
Tonko represents all of Albany and Schenectady Counties and parts of Rensselaer, Saratoga and Montgomery Counties, including Albany, Amsterdam, Schenectady, Troy and Saratoga Springs.

He serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, as Ranking Member of its Subcommittee on Environment and a member of its Energy and Oversight & Investigations subcommittees, and was selected for the House Budget Committee in the 119th Congress; he previously served on the Natural Resources, Education and Labor, and Science, Space, and Technology committees.
He is Democratic Deputy Whip for Policy and co-chairs the Sustainable Energy and Environment Coalition and the Addiction, Treatment, and Recovery Caucus.
